name: office filing
description: Read top to bottom. The first rule whose conditions all hold is the one that files the attachment; nothing below it is consulted. An attachment that matches no rule goes to unsorted/ with the reason recorded, because a wrong folder is harder to find than an unsorted one.

rules.name: invoices
rules.description: Anything calling itself an invoice, whoever it is from. First in the list on purpose: an invoice from the bank is still an invoice, and this rule is above the bank rule that would otherwise claim it.

rules.name: receipts
rules.description: Payment confirmations. Kept separate from invoices because they are filed for different reasons.

rules.name: bank-statements
rules.description: Everything else from the bank. Sender-based, because statement subjects are not worth matching on.

rules.name: contracts
rules.description: Matched on the attachment's own filename rather than the subject, because the covering email usually says nothing useful.

rules.name: site-photos
rules.description: Job photos, filed under the crew that sent them. `{sender_local}` is the part of the address before the @, so photos from crew@sunfield-installations.example land in photos/crew.

rules.name: supplier-paperwork
rules.description: The catch-for-one-sender rule: anything else from a supplier we deal with often, filed under their domain. Note this is last, so their invoices still go to invoices/.
